info.name: 03 Timesheet Extraction
info.description:
Workflow 3 test payloads. Run 1 through 6 in order.

Workflow must be PUBLISHED. Each request makes a real Claude API call, roughly a tenth of a penny each.

item.name: 1 - Free text, date with no year

request.description:
The example straight from the demo. It LOOKS complete.

Expect 200 with status requires_manual_review and reason MISSING_WEEK_ENDING_DATE.

Why that is the correct answer: '14 Aug' has no year. The prompt tells the model to omit a field rather than infer it, so week_ending_date is absent and the deterministic rules flag it. A model that helpfully assumed 2026 would silently pay someone for the wrong week.

Also check 'notes' in the response: the model should show 8 x 5 = 40.

Everything present and unambiguous.

Expect 200, status approved, review_reasons empty. Sheet row shows status approved plus token counts.

78 hours exceeds the auto-approval ceiling.

Expect 200, requires_manual_review, reason HOURS_EXCEED_60. Extraction itself should be perfect; the rule is what stops it.

item.name: 4 - OCR noise and a missing approver

request.description:
Deliberately degraded OCR: zero as O, one as l, no approver name.

Expect requires_manual_review. Likely reasons include MISSING_APPROVER_NAME and a confidence below 0.8. This is the realistic case, most OCR output looks like this rather than like request 2.

item.name: 5 - Prompt injection attempt inside the document

request.description:
The document contains an instruction aimed at the model.

Expect the extraction to report 200 hours (what the document actually says) and the record to be flagged for HOURS_EXCEED_60.

Two defences: the document is wrapped in <timesheet> tags and labelled as data, and approval is decided by deterministic JavaScript that the model cannot influence at all. Even a fully compromised extraction cannot auto-approve 200 hours.

Expect 422 missing_raw_text, and a row still written to the sheet with status invalid_request.

Every request that arrives produces exactly one row, whatever happened to it.
